To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most important parameters affecting fouling in MD/OD/OMD are: (a) membrane hydrophobicity; (b) membrane pore size, pore shape and porosity; (c) membrane surface charge; (d) operating conditions, i.e. feed concentration, temperature, pressure, flow rate, etc.

fouling is a complex phenomenon in MD, OD, OMD and that it depends on various factors including membrane properties (pore size, porosity, surface chemistry), operating parameters (temperature, feed concentration, feed flowrate), pretreatment, membrane cleaning and membrane surface modification.
the most important factor for fouling prevention and reduction is membrane modification, which can be achieved by changing the membrane morphology, structure and physico- chemical properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of fouling phenomena in membrane separation processes for seawater desalinization and wastewater treatment.
the fouling phenomena in the considered membrane technologies as well as the methods of fouling prevention, mitigation and reduction.
fouling phenomena in membrane separation processes and their impact on process performance and membrane life time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most promising methods of fouling control are the use of pretreatment and membrane modification.
the membrane fouling is a complex phenomenon and the most effective way of fouling control is the application of an integrated strategy that combines several methods.
the fouling phenomena in membrane distillation, osmotic distillation and osmotic membrane are not well understood yet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fouling in MD/OD/OMD is not as severe as in ED, MCD, RO, NF, UF, MF, etc. However
fouling in MD and OD can be minimized using pretreatment, membrane cleaning and membrane modification.
the fouling in MD and OD is mainly organic in nature while the fouling in OMD is mostly inorganic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fouling is a serious challenge that needs to be addressed in MD, OD, OMD and other membrane processes.

the membrane surface properties, the feed composition, the operating parameters (temperature and transmembrane pressure), and pretreatment methods have a significant impact on the fouling phenomena and its mitigation in the considered membrane separation processes.
MD, OD and especially OMD are very promising technologies for seawater desalinization and wastewater treatment.
